title: Certificate of competency: three distinct statutory powers had been merged into one Part IV citation
candidate_claim: GPT review pass 2A authorised a multi-Part answer for QB9_D#q6's certificate-of-competency limb, directing that grant, issuing-authority withdrawal and Central Government suspension be distinguished rather than forced into Part IV, and that the powers be described separately rather than merged.
candidate_verdict: UPHELD. The card cited 'MS Act 2025, Part IV (formerly 1958 Sec 76 & 87) ... exact 2025 section numbers pending verification' for the whole of issuance, control and suspension. Two defects follow. Part IV does not contain the Central Government's suspension power at all - that is s.312, in Part XV - so a Part IV citation cannot reach it. And the card's CE Relevance paragraph attributed the inquiry-and-suspend power to 'the DGS' under 'the broad powers of the MS Act', which is neither of the two authorities the Act actually names.

authority.how_read: The Act's text layer was extracted in full: 118 pages, 393,583 characters. Every section cited below was resolved and read directly from that text and occurs exactly once as an operative section. Pass 2A's mapping was treated as an AUTHORISATION, not as evidence, and independently re-verified before anything was written candidate-facing.
authority.extraction_hazards: TWO, recorded because one produced a false negative. (1) The Act's PDF separates a section number from its text with a 0x03 CONTROL BYTE as well as with a space, so a '^[0-9]+[.]\s' scan under-reports: s.319 was reported NOT FOUND on the first pass and is present exactly as authorised. A negative from a text scan is only evidence once the scan is proved able to find a positive. (2) The s.281(2) penalty table renumbers its rows 1..N, so a naive scan resolves 'section 15' to a table row about s.139; table rows must be excluded before a section number is resolved.
authority.part_structure: Verified from the Act: I ss.1-3; II ss.4-13; III ss.14-44; IV ss.45-53; V ss.54-113; VI ss.114-130; VII ss.131-143; VIII ss.144-152; IX ss.153-222; X ss.223-230; XI ss.231-232; XII ss.233-260; XIII ss.261-280; XIV ss.281-292; XV ss.293-324; XVI s.325.
authority.grant: s.46(1): 'An officer notified by the Central Government as the issuing authority shall, subject to the provisions of the Standards of Training, Certification and Watchkeeping for Seafarers Convention, grant a certificate of competency or certificate of proficiency for different grades of seafarers with such requirements and procedures as may be prescribed.' Part IV, verified as ss.45-53.
authority.issuing_authority_withdrawal: s.48(6): if it appears to the issuing authority that a holder obtained the certificate on false or erroneous information, or is guilty of indiscipline or misconduct, incompetency, or any act of omission or commission or compromise to safety, security or prevention of pollution, it may AFTER DUE INVESTIGATION, by order, withdraw, suspend or cancel it; the proviso requires a reasonable opportunity of being heard. s.48(7): appeal before the officer the Central Government notifies as appellate authority.
authority.central_government_suspension: s.312, PART XV: the Central Government may by order cancel or suspend any certificate granted under the Act to any seafarer for a specified period where (a) an inquiry report or investigation report reveals incompetency or misconduct, (b) in a case of collision the seafarer failed to render assistance, (c) the seafarer has been convicted of an offence under the Act or a non-bailable offence under any other law in or outside India, (d) a casualty was caused by the seafarer's wrongful act or default, or (e) the seafarer contravenes the Act; proviso requires an opportunity of being heard. Part XV is ss.293-324, so this is NOT reachable by a Part IV citation.
authority.s62_5_not_used: The brief permitted s.62(5) to be mentioned only if already directly relevant to an engagement-rule discussion on this card. The card's s.62 treatment concerns the RPSL delegation, not engagement-rule violations, so s.62(5) was NOT introduced.

changed_propositions: REG-BOX: 'MS Act 2025, Part IV (formerly 1958 Sec 76 & 87) - Regulates the legal issuance, control, and potential suspension of Certificates of Competency (CoC); exact 2025 section numbers pending verification.' -> 'MS Act 2025 - s.46(1), s.48(6)-(7) (Part IV); s.312 (Part XV)', described as THREE DISTINCT POWERS: grant, issuing-authority withdrawal with its hearing and appeal, and Central Government suspension with its five grounds. The unverifiable 1958 Sec 76 & 87 equivalence is dropped rather than strengthened.

CE Relevance paragraph, in BOTH of its copies on this card - the answer body and the deep-dive block: 'under the broad powers of the MS Act, the DGS retains the statutory right to conduct inquiries, suspend, or cancel a Chief Engineer's Certificate of Competency (CoC) if found guilty of gross negligence or professional misconduct during a maritime casualty' -> the two separate powers named and attributed correctly, to the ISSUING AUTHORITY under s.48(6)-(7) and to the CENTRAL GOVERNMENT under s.312, with the express warning that merging them is a common oral error.
